name: Engineering
migratedFrom: guides218.json professions[3] (2026-11-04), rewritten into a full course on 2026-11-12

overview.lead: Engineers build explosives, gadgets and devices. Forever adds explosives that anyone can use, satchel bombs for the thrown slot and belts for every armor type.

points.text: Mining supplies most of the materials.
The Gnome racial no longer adds Engineering skill; it now makes devices fail and backfire less often.

heldBack.text: Many new engineering recipes use alchemy materials.
heldBack.reason: No graded engineering fact names the alchemy materials.

101.summary: What Engineering makes in Forever, its camp objects and how to level it.

steps.text: Open the professions window with K, then search or filter the recipe list and track a recipe in the objectives frame.
Place your first engineering camp object at skill 20, the second at 140 and the Anarchist's Workbench at 300. The skill-140 blueprint drops from Sneed in the Deadmines.
Keep your Engineering skill up as you level: Icy Veins says some gadgets now scale with it.
As a Gnome, expect fewer failures and backfires rather than extra skill: Engineering Specialization now cuts that rate by 20%.
Sit at the camp for at least 1 minute to get its buff. A basic campsite holds 3 camp features, one per player, so agree in the group who places what.

mistakes.mistake: Counting on the Gnome racial for extra Engineering skill.
mistakes.fix: It no longer adds skill. It cuts the failure and backfire rate of engineering devices by 20%.

steps.text: Train Journeyman at skill 50 and level 10, Expert at skill 125 and level 20, and Artisan at skill 200 and level 35. 300 is the cap.
Build Merchant's Favor by filling Waylaid Crates and handing the sealed crates to Marcy Baker at Three Corners in western Redridge. Craftsman's Writs add reputation.
Your first Favor recipe can come early: SAF-T Dynamite costs 45 Merchant's Favor at skill 25.
Reaching 150, 225 and 300 for the first time in a craft each earns 1 Legacy point. Performance Bonus adds extra Merchant's Favor, and Working Overtime improves your skill-up chance.
Plan the Goblin or Gnomish choice. Forever guides list the same choice as Classic 1.12, where a quest at skill 200 decides it and switching means unlearning.
At 300, earn the certification item that unlocks your profession title. Alliance players get it from the Azeroth Commerce Authority.

mistakes.mistake: Waiting at the Journeyman cap of 150 before training Expert.
mistakes.fix: Expert needs skill 125 and level 20, so train it between 125 and 150.

mistakes.mistake: Picking Goblin or Gnomish without looking at the devices.
mistakes.fix: Choose by what you want: in Classic 1.12 Goblin engineers get Dimensional Ripper - Everlook, Gnomish engineers get Ultrasafe Transporter: Gadgetzan and World Enlarger, and switching means unlearning.

201.summary: Gear, explosives for the raid, and the market.

chapters.title: Belts and the Emergency Field Cloak

steps.text: Make a Clanking Cord belt for your armor type: engineers can make one for each.
Plan for the Emergency Field Cloak if you want an invisibility trinket. The recipe needs Honored and 270 Favor, and the trinket is Bind on Pickup.

mistakes.mistake: Promising a guildmate an Emergency Field Cloak.
mistakes.fix: It is Bind on Pickup: only the engineer who makes it can use it.

steps.text: Hand SAF-T explosives such as SAF-T Dynamite out to the group: non-engineers can use them.
Satchel bombs go in the thrown-weapon slot and run from Copper up to Dark Iron, which needs skill 285 and Honored.
Treat Goblin Sapper Charge, Thorium Grenade and Dark Iron Bomb as Classic 1.12 raid explosives until someone checks them in Forever.

mistakes.fix: Non-engineers can use SAF-T explosives, so an engineer can hand them out to the group.

steps.text: SAF-T explosives work for anyone, so they sell beyond other engineers. Test satchel bombs and gadgets once live prices settle. Trading is subject to Blizzard policy.
Check the Auction House before you sell surplus crafts to a vendor: Blizzard's beta notes say many profession-made items sell to vendors for less.

mistakes.mistake: Selling surplus crafts to a vendor out of Classic habit.
mistakes.fix: Many profession-made items sell to vendors for less in Forever, so compare the Auction House first.
